## Immunomodulatory Role of Tenascin-C in Myocarditis and Inflammatory Cardiomyopathy

- Gap status: unmet
- Material use: supporting

### Useful material

This study provides a mechanistic framework for how gut microbiota can trigger autoimmune myocarditis, specifically citing *Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron* where bacterial beta-galactosidase shares sequence homology with cardiac MyHC-α, inducing Th17 polarization. It also details a downstream signaling pathway in myocarditis involving Tenascin-C (TN-C) activating dendritic cells via TLR4 to produce IL-6, IL-1β, and GM-CSF, driving Th17 differentiation.

### Supporting material

General triggers of myocarditis including viruses (CVB3, SARS-CoV-2) and immune checkpoint inhibitors; description of central and peripheral immune tolerance mechanisms; TN-C as a biomarker for disease activity and prognosis.

Open point: The supplied text does not mention *Prevotella spp.*, the FMT-LUMINate study, or any specific antigens, metabolites, or downstream signaling pathways associated with *Prevotella*-induced myocarditis. The specific molecular mechanism requested in the gap question remains unidentified in this material.
